issues.issue: The insurer's right to strip Policy Value or demand insurability is triggered when the Net Amount at Risk "exceeds our guidelines and limitations that may be in effect" — an external, undisclosed and unilaterally variable standard.
The closing text is broken: "You are limited to one surrender charges for this policy" is not a sentence, and the limit on changes per Policy Year has been displaced into a stray heading.
The Monthly Guarantee Premium may be modified on "a change in risk classification," but no mechanism anywhere fixes how the revised premium is computed or when Risk Classification can change.

This makes the post-age-100 Death Benefit the greater of Total Face Amount or Policy Value, dropping the Minimum Death Benefit Percentage multiplier that Section 6 (c053) applies, although Section 8 opens by saying the benefit is determined "in the same respect as specified in Section 6."

"We will not accept any further premium payments" after the Age 100 Anniversary cannot be reconciled with Section 11 (c087), which allows a policy in default to be cured only by additional premiums or debt repayment, and with Section 13 reinstatement.
Post-age-100 default is defined here, but Section 11's cure mechanism (c087) contemplates payment of additional premiums, which c061 forbids after the Age 100 Anniversary.

Component (d) charges for "any applicable Additional Ratings shown in Section 1," but Section 1 records Additional Ratings as "Not Applicable" while the acceptance form states the base policy is rated (c168).

The rating factors listed here (sex, Age, Risk Classification, Basic and Supplemental Face Amount, Net Amount at Risk, duration) are an enumeration whose exclusivity is left open, and "duration that the coverage has been in force" is not tied to any table.

This list of factors for rates "as of the Policy Date" differs from the wholly different list governing rates thereafter in the next paragraph (c070), leaving it unclear which controls a re-determination.

"Such rates will be based on our expectations of future mortality, persistency, investment earnings, expense experience, capital and reserve requirements, and tax assumptions" is an enumerated list with no catch-all, so whether the insurer may set COI rates on factors outside the list — and what "based on" requires — is squarely contestable.
The constrained rate formula here cannot be squared with the Schedule footnote asserting an unqualified "right to change ... the amount of cost of insurance deducted under the policy" (c011).

"On a basis that does not discriminate unfairly within any class of insureds" leaves "class of insureds" undefined and "unfairly" unmeasured, and "we will not ... recoup prior losses" gives no test for when a rate increase does so.
The limits on re-determination stated here are contradicted by the Schedule footnote reserving an unrestricted right to change the cost of insurance deducted (c011).

The crediting sentence is broken mid-line so that the standard ("anticipation of future investment earnings, mortality, persistency, expense and administrative costs, and taxes") floats free of the grant of "sole discretion" to change rates, leaving it unclear whether that standard constrains the discretion.
The Additional Interest table is internally garbled — a middle band of "50%" against a top band of "4.00%" — so the rate actually payable in each band cannot be read off the provision.
The instruction not to process premiums that would disqualify the policy sits against Section 4's promise that "in no event" will a premium needed to prevent termination be refused (c041).

The middle of the paragraph is unreadable ("Unless we agree oth ===gre-subject-to-the-Maximum-Annual-Premium-shol 6 Overloan Protection"), so the Maximum Annual Premium limit and the Overloan cut-off cannot be stated from the text.
This debt-based default and its premium cure must be read with Section 8 (c061), which bars acceptance of any premium after the Age 100 Anniversary while expressly keeping default alive.

The opening of the Reduced Paid-Up Benefit is destroyed ("-after-this.policy.has..been..in-force.for.at.least.one.full ~=lapsed-to-a- -"), so the conditions for and nature of the election cannot be determined from the provision.
The exclusive list of automatic termination events omits the Maturity Date, although Section 1 fixes a Maturity Date of October 12, 2035 and Section 3 defines it as a policy term.

The provision begins mid-sentence ("request. A loan may not be taken after you have exercised Overloan Protecti"), so the operative grant of the right to take a loan and its conditions are missing from the text.

"A change in the Interest Rate" is capitalised but undefined, and could mean the credited interest rate under Section 9 or the policy loan interest rate under the surrounding Loan Interest Charged provision.

The right to repay Policy Debt "at any time prior to the death of the Insured and while the policy is in force" conflicts with the Overloan Protection bullet stating that no loan repayments will be allowed (c108).

Condition 2 requires that the Policy Debt "is equal to 96% of the Policy Value," a knife-edge test that cannot be squared with the next paragraph's assumption that the loan balance may be "in excess of 96% of the Policy Value" when the option is exercised (c101).
